questions.question: Which language should the Bunny Log frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed JavaScript for a maintainable interactive application.

questions.question: Which framework should the Bunny Log frontend use?

options.label: React
options.description: A component-based framework with a broad ecosystem.

options.label: Vue
options.description: A progressive framework with approachable component authoring.

options.label: Svelte
options.description: A compiler-based framework for lean interactive interfaces.

options.label: Angular
options.description: A full-featured framework with an integrated application platform.

questions.question: What should the Bunny Log frontend include?
questions.answer: Warm cream/off-white and sage/brown palette; rabbit-icon logo; left navigation for Home, Daily Log, Food, Weight, Health, Memories, and Settings; time-aware dashboard greeting, rabbit profile, daily check-in markers, summary cards, weight graph, and prominent Log Today action; calendar with paw indicators and selected-day details; food tracking, favorites, and weekly overview; weight chart; health records and reminders; scrapbook photo gallery with captions; right-side slide-in logging panel; playful rabbit and button interactions; responsive layouts and accessible interactions.
questions.recommendedChoice: Warm cream/off-white and sage/brown palette; rabbit-icon logo; left navigation for Home, Daily Log, Food, Weight, Health, Memories, and Settings; time-aware dashboard greeting, rabbit profile, daily check-in markers, summary cards, weight graph, and prominent Log Today action; calendar with paw indicators and selected-day details; food tracking, favorites, and weekly overview; weight chart; health records and reminders; scrapbook photo gallery with captions; right-side slide-in logging panel; playful rabbit and button interactions; responsive layouts and accessible interactions.

questions.question: Which language should the Bunny Log backend API use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Share the JavaScript ecosystem across frontend and API.

options.label: Python
options.description: Use Python for API development and data-oriented workflows.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: Use .NET for a strongly typed API service.

questions.question: Which framework should the Bunny Log backend API use?

options.label: Express
options.description: A minimal, widely used Node.js API framework.

options.label: NestJS
options.description: A structured TypeScript framework for larger APIs.

questions.question: What should the Bunny Log backend API support?
questions.answer: Persist rabbit profiles, daily care logs, food entries and favorites, weight measurements, health records and reminders, and scrapbook photo metadata; provide APIs to create, read, update, and delete these records; store photo files in Blob Storage.
questions.recommendedChoice: Persist rabbit profiles, daily care logs, food entries and favorites, weight measurements, health records and reminders, and scrapbook photo metadata; provide APIs to create, read, update, and delete these records; store photo files in Blob Storage.

questions.question: Which data stores should Bunny Log use?

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational storage for profiles, logs, measurements, and health records.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Object storage for scrapbook photos and other uploaded media.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use only transient or browser-local data; no managed datastore.

questions.question: Should users sign in to access Bunny Log's application features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require users to sign in before accessing application features.

options.label: No
options.description: Keep application features available without user sign-in.
